notes.heading: Choose an invariant that describes the processed prefix
paragraphs: A useful invariant says exactly what is true before each iteration and ties that statement to the amount of input already processed. For an average, retain both a total and a count. For a search, specify what has been ruled out. For a repeated subtraction loop, a quantity that decreases is only a termination argument if it cannot decrease indefinitely in the permitted domain. Empty input needs a separate contract when an operation such as division or selecting the first element is required. Test equality and boundary cases as deliberately as typical inputs.

questions.prompt: An algorithm sets total=0 and count=0, then adds each value in [2, 0, 7] to total and increments count. Trace the states and explain why total/count must not be evaluated before processing an empty list.
questions.answer: The states are (2,1), (2,2), (9,3); the final mean is 3. With no elements the count is zero, so the mean needs an explicit undefined/error result.
solution: Accumulate one value and one count per iteration.
Divide only when count is positive; the invariant is that total sums the count processed values.
markingPoints: Identify division by zero for empty input.

questions.prompt: A loop repeatedly executes x=x-2 while x!=0. Does it terminate for every nonnegative integer input? Give a failing input and a corrected precondition if the body is kept unchanged.
questions.answer: No. Starting at 3 gives 3,1,-1,-3,... and never reaches zero. Requiring an even nonnegative integer ensures termination.
solution: Subtracting 2 preserves parity; an odd value cannot become zero.
For even nonnegative x, x/2 is a nonnegative integer that decreases by one each iteration.
markingPoints: Give the decreasing nonnegative termination measure.

questions.prompt: A zero-indexed list has four elements. A loop begins i=0, reads a[i], increments i, and repeats while i<=4. Identify the invalid access and repair the bound.
questions.answer: The loop attempts a[4], which is outside indices 0 through 3. Use a pre-test loop with condition i<4, or i<length(a).
solution: List the valid indices before tracing the final iteration.
Use a strict upper bound and check the condition before every read.
